newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis said to issue $1 bln shares on NYSE.
newsitem.headline: Israelis said to issue $1 bln shares on NYSE.

text.p: Sources on Wall Street told Finance Minister Dan Meridor that Israeli companies will issue about $1 billion in shares in the United States in 1996, the Treasury said.

"The number of Israeli companies issuing shares in New York and the success of these offerings are further witness to the faith foreign investors have in Israel's economy and in Israeli companies," a Treasury spokesman quoted Meridor as saying during a visit to Wall Street.
Meridor is in the United States to attend the International Monetary Fund (IMF) conference in Washington.

Meridor was told that since the beginning of the year Israeli companies had issued $750 million in shares in the United States. Nearly 100 Israeli securities are listed in the United States, mostly on Nasdaq.
Treasury sources said Meridor was encouraged by the interest shown by foreign investors in Israel.
He criticised those foreign investors who expect the government to give them incentives for capital investment.

Meridor said he was surprised that "those same people who talk in favour of massive privatisation and less government intervention in the economy, request with the same breath special government assistance."
The new government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has decided to cut back on capital investment grants given to local and foreign investors from 1997.
